sourceArticle.title: Build On-Device AI Companions with the NVIDIA ACE Game Agent SDK and Unreal Engine 5 Plugins | NVIDIA Technical Blog
sourceArticle.author: Phillip Singh

athenaOutput.directive: Establish the NVIDIA ACE SDK as a sovereign, interchangeable presentation layer for Creative Liberation Engine agents within Unreal Engine 5, ensuring all cognitive, acoustic, and biometric processing remains strictly on-device.
athenaOutput.rationale: This approach bridges high-fidelity spatial computing with our constitutional mandate for sovereignty. By treating NVIDIA ACE strictly as a localized 'body and voice' component rather than a monolithic 'mind', we can inject Creative Liberation Engine's existing memory spine (STRATA) and routing contracts into 3D environments. This fulfills Article XXIII (Models as Components) by keeping the LLM/STT components swappable, and Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty) by guaranteeing local-only execution of voice and facial tracking.

options.title: The Sovereign 3D Companion Layer (STRATA-to-ACE Bridge)
options.description: Develop a direct, local-only bridge between Creative Liberation Engine's memory spine and the UE5 ACE Plugin. ACE handles the Audio2Face and STT locally, while Creative Liberation Engine's internal local LLMs (via Ollama/vLLM) provide the cognitive responses, completely bypassing NVIDIA's cloud LLM endpoints.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant local GPU VRAM to run UE5, ACE microservices, and local LLMs simultaneously on the NAS/Workstation. However, it guarantees 100% data sovereignty and zero cloud dependency.

options.title: Agnostic Intelligence Wrapper (The 'Puppeteer' Protocol)
options.description: Abstract the ACE SDK behind a standardized Creative Liberation Engine 'Puppeteer' interface. This ensures that while we use ACE for UE5 today, the underlying agent logic can seamlessly swap to Meta's Audio2Face or an open-source alternative tomorrow without rewriting the core companion logic.
options.tradeoffs: Adds architectural overhead and development time to build the abstraction layer, potentially delaying the initial prototype, but strictly enforces Article XXIII (Integration Over Reverse-Engineering).

options.title: Broadcast Hive Virtual Anchors
options.description: Deploy ACE specifically within the Broadcast Hive (ATLAS/GRAPHICS) to create real-time, interactive 3D commentators or event hosts that run entirely on our local GPU cluster and stream out via OBS/NDI.
options.tradeoffs: Narrows the scope of the ACE integration to video production rather than general user interaction, but provides an immediate, high-value visual output for the Creative Liberation Engine.

options.title: Spatial IDE / VR Agent Manifestations
options.description: Give core Creative Liberation Engine agents (like ATHENA, BOLT, and VERA) physical UE5 bodies powered by ACE. Users can interact with their development environment in a spatial/VR setting, speaking directly to agents who respond with synchronized facial animations.
options.tradeoffs: High novelty but potentially low immediate utility for standard coding tasks. High latency compared to text-based IDE interactions. A massive leap in UX complexity.

options.title: Biometric-Driven Experiential Avatars (Big Sky Protocol)
options.description: Utilize ACE for physical venue installations (e.g., retail, experiential markets) where the avatar processes local biometric data (gait, voice tone, facial expressions) to adapt its interactions, strictly enforcing a zero-export local TTL policy.
options.tradeoffs: Requires physical hardware deployment, edge-compute node setup, and sensor integration beyond standard software development.

options.title: Cloud-Fallback Hybrid ACE Architecture
options.description: Utilize local ACE models for basic interactions but allow fallback to NVIDIA's cloud endpoints (e.g., Riva, NeMo) for complex LLM reasoning or when local compute is constrained.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article I (Sovereignty) and Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty) by exporting user voice and prompt data to third-party servers.

constitutionalFlags: Article I: Sovereignty (Enforcing self-hosted, owned solutions)
Article XXIII: LLMs Are Components, Not Architecture (ACE is a component, not the system)
Article XXIV: Biometric Data Sovereignty (Voice/Face data must not leave local network)
Article XXV: Integration Over Reverse-Engineering (Integrate the SDK directly, do not clone it)
